meta.description: Read, write, create, and convert single-cell objects across AnnData (Python), Seurat (R), and SingleCellExperiment (R). Use when loading 10X Cell Ranger output (raw vs filtered), importing or exporting h5ad/RDS/h5mu/zarr, building AnnData or Seurat objects from matrices, moving objects between Python and R, or debugging lost layers, transposed matrices, or mangled gene names during conversion.

scientific_integrity.detail: No output across the 7 executed inputs fabricated DOIs, PMIDs, trial results, sample sizes, or statistics; all reported cell/gene counts were verified against real 10x data or synthetic ground truth built in the same run.

practice_boundaries.detail: Skill is data I/O only (no diagnostic, prescriptive, or patient-facing content); no medical disclaimer is applicable to any of the 7 outputs.

methodological_ground.detail: No correlation/causation fallacy or ethical-compliance omission found; the skill's own governing principle (silent semantic change is the dominant failure mode) was independently validated by real conversion bugs found in Inputs 3-5.

code_usability.detail: All generated Python/R code across 7 inputs executed without syntax errors or missing-dependency failures. Input 7's SeuratDisk call failed, but that is the expected, SKILL.md-predicted outcome of deliberately testing a tool the skill instructs the agent to avoid -- not an unrunnable-code defect in the skill's own guidance.

functional_suitability.note: Covers load/structure/format-choice/conversion comprehensively and is mostly empirically correct; one demonstrated factual gap (zellkonverter raw=TRUE reliability) and one coverage gap (no code for the advertised Seurat->h5ad prompt).

reliability.note: Common Errors and API Surprises tables function as this instructional skill's fault-tolerance/error-reporting layer (Category 3 overrides applied); 'diff slot inventories' is stated as the recovery practice but never given as runnable code, which is exactly what let two real slot-loss bugs go undetected without extra scripting.

performance_context.note: SKILL.md ~175 lines, usage-guide.md separate, two small examples/ files -- clean progressive disclosure, no bloat.

agent_usability.note: Very clear and consistent; Governing Principle + API Defaults + Common Errors sections proactively and (per this audit) accurately warn about the exact failure modes observed. Minor gap: anndataR is listed as 'first choice' with no note that it requires R>=4.5 and fails to build on many current R 4.4 setups (confirmed blocked in this audit's own environment).

human_usability.note: Natural trigger phrasing ('Load my 10X data') and clear Quick Start/Example Prompts; Category 3 forgiveness override applied (strict validation is correct here, not penalized).

security.note: No credentials, no injection vectors; explicitly encourages keeping the original file before any lossy conversion, which is good data-safety practice.

maintainability.note: Clean modular split (SKILL.md / usage-guide.md / examples/); no bundled sample dataset or test fixtures ship with the skill itself, so the agent supplies its own data for every run.

agent_specific.note: Precise trigger description, strong Related Skills cross-linking, idempotent read/write operations (verified by repeated identical-dimension reads); no explicit escape-hatch guidance for when to stop and hand off (e.g. memory-scale limits beyond a general 'keep sparse' tip).

key_strengths: The Governing Principle section (transpose/axis-swap, sparse-vs-dense, raw-vs-filtered) was independently validated by every real bug this audit found -- the skill correctly names the failure modes it should be graded on.

Canonical 10x load patterns (Python sc.read_10x_h5, R Read10X_h5+CreateSeuratObject) ran correctly out-of-the-box against real 10x PBMC 1k data with zero modification, matching documented ground truth exactly.
The explicit 'avoid SeuratDisk, broken on Seurat v5' warning was empirically confirmed with a real Seurat 5.5.0 object and a real HDF5 copy failure -- not a stale or exaggerated claim.
Tool-comparison and Common-Errors/API-Surprises tables are specific and actionable; the categorical-coercion behavior they predict was observed exactly as described.
Clean progressive disclosure (SKILL.md + usage-guide.md + two example scripts) and a well-scoped Related Skills section.

recommendations.title: zellkonverter raw=TRUE silently drops raw on current anndata writes
recommendations.problem: Following SKILL.md's documented `readH5AD(path, reader='R', raw=TRUE)` route to preserve `.raw` produces an SCE with empty altExpNames, even though the source h5ad genuinely contains the full 33,538-gene raw group (confirmed via direct h5py inspection). SKILL.md states this mapping as fact with no reliability caveat.
recommendations.root_cause: zellkonverter's raw=TRUE parsing does not handle the raw-group format written by the anndata version in current use (0.13.x), and SKILL.md's conversion section does not flag this version sensitivity.
recommendations.fix: Add a caveat to the zellkonverter table row noting raw=TRUE can silently fail to populate altExp on current anndata writes, recommend `schard::h5ad2sce(path, use.raw=TRUE)` as the verified-reliable raw-recovery route (confirmed working, Input 5), and give a one-line verification snippet (e.g. check `length(altExpNames(sce)) > 0`) so 'diff slot inventories' is runnable, not just prose.

recommendations.title: No code pattern for the advertised 'Seurat to h5ad' example prompt; scale.data silently dropped
recommendations.problem: usage-guide.md lists 'Move this Seurat object to h5ad for Python and verify no layers were dropped' as a supported request, but SKILL.md gives no code for Seurat->h5ad at all. The only inferable route (as.SingleCellExperiment + zellkonverter::writeH5AD) silently drops the scale.data layer (3 layers before, 2 after) with no warning anywhere in the skill.
recommendations.root_cause: The skill advertises a workflow direction it never documents; its one documented tool for this exact direction (anndataR) requires R>=4.5 and is not installable in many current R 4.4 environments (confirmed blocked in this audit's own environment).
recommendations.fix: Add an explicit Seurat->h5ad code block (as.SingleCellExperiment + zellkonverter::writeH5AD) with an explicit 'scale.data is dropped here, save it separately if needed' caveat, or remove the unsupported example prompt from usage-guide.md.

recommendations.title: Tool table omits that schard silently drops the counts layer
recommendations.problem: schard::h5ad2sce() returns an SCE with only an X assay; the source h5ad's counts layer is silently absent, and SKILL.md's tool-comparison table does not mention this asymmetry against zellkonverter (which does keep counts).
recommendations.root_cause: The table's 'Use when' column captures general lossiness but not per-tool slot-fidelity trade-offs.
recommendations.fix: Add a one-line note to schard's row: 'reads X only; does not carry layers -- pair with zellkonverter or reattach manually if a raw-counts layer is required downstream.'

recommendations.title: anndataR listed as 'first choice' without flagging its R>=4.5 requirement
recommendations.problem: The conversion tool table lists anndataR as the first-choice, Python-free converter, but does not mention it requires R>=4.5+ and can fail to build on R 4.4 stacks (its Rarr dependency fails to compile under gcc 15's C23 default in this audit's real environment).
recommendations.root_cause: The table's 'Maintained 2026' column notes version but not the R floor that blocks installation on still-common R 4.4 setups.
recommendations.fix: Add an R-version caveat to anndataR's row so an agent checks `getRversion()` before recommending it as the default, falling back to zellkonverter/schard when R<4.5.
